div.head:
No. 939
Editorial Note
div.p: In accordance with the desire of Secretary Dulles and Under Secretary Hoover to keep the distribution of communications about the proposed Arab-Israel settlement to an absolute minimum, the Acting Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern, South Asian, and African Affairs, John D. Jernegan, suggested in a memorandum dated December 20 to the Director of the Executive Secretariat, Walter K. Scott, that the distribution of these materials within the Department of State should be restricted to the following: three copies for the Executive Secretariat to enable it to maintain a basic file as well as to provide the Secretary and the Under Secretary with individual copies of each document; one copy for the information of Deputy Under Secretary of State Robert Murphy; and three copies for the Bureau of Near Eastern, South Asian, and African Affairs to enable it to maintain a basic file as well as to provide one copy for the joint use of the Assistant and Deputy Assistant Secretary and one copy for the files of Francis H. Russell. To facilitate the distribution of these materials, Jernegan also suggested that these documents be captioned “Limited Distribution—Alpha”. (NEA files, lot 59 D 518, “Washington Talks, Jan.–Feb. 1955: Memos, etc. preceding actual meetings (Dated 11/15/54 thru 1/27/55)”)

Scott approved Jernegan’s suggestions and issued appropriate instructions on December 21. (Memorandum by Walter K. Scott to Paul E. Pfeiffer, Chief of the Telegraph Branch, and to Walter H. Anderson, Chief of the Records Branch, Office of Communications
and Records; S/S–NEA files, lot 61 D 417, “Alpha Volume 1”) On December 21, Scott also approved the transmittal of instructions to the Chiefs of Mission at Amman, Ankara, Baghdad, Beirut, Cairo, Damascus, Jerusalem, Jidda, London, and Tel Aviv informing them that thenceforth any communications regarding the Arab-Israel settlement should be classified Top Secret, captioned Limit Distribution, given the code word “Alpha”, and should receive minimal circulation within their missions. (Circular telegram 319, December 21; 684A.86/12–2154)
